shots.prompt: Slow push in on a vaudeville theatre marquee at night, bulbs flickering on in sequence around lettering that reads "EVERYTHING'S FINE". Rain-slick pavement below catches the bulb light. The camera moves continuously throughout, never settling.

Heavy stage curtain rises steadily to reveal an empty vaudeville stage with footlights burning. Dust drifts in the beam. The curtain is still rising as the shot ends — continuous upward motion, no hold.

Seth strides on from stage left in a confident soft-shoe, arms swinging wide, and arrives centre stage already settled into a grin, one hand raised to the audience. Ake's ochre is the only warm colour anywhere in frame.

Seth performs to the house, gesturing broadly with a can of Diet Coke raised like a champagne flute, weight shifting foot to foot in a steady vaudeville rhythm. Continuous performance, never a frozen pose.
Behind Seth a tall status board of round indicator lamps clicks over one by one to a calm even glow, each lamp lighting in sequence. Seth turns to admire it, still moving.
A single thin ribbon of smoke rises steadily from behind the status board, unnoticed. Seth continues his soft-shoe downstage, oblivious, the smoke climbing throughout the shot.

The full troupe swings into a chorus line across the stage — Seth, Wilson the picket fence, Cadbury the butler and Ake's fishbowl on its wheeled dolly — all moving together in a side-stepping kick, arms linked where arms exist. Ake's ochre is the only warm colour.
The chorus line kicks in unison, Ake's dolly rolling with them and the water in his bowl sloshing visibly up the glass with each kick. Continuous rhythmic motion throughout.

The troupe clears and Wilson the living picket fence rolls forward alone, leaning slowly over a stage rail, his segmented metal arms folding on the top rail, the miniature server rack swinging gently from its chain. His two cartoon eyes float in the deep shadow under the bucket hat brim.

Wilson gesticulates unhurriedly with one segmented arm, tipping the bucket hat back with the other, the whole fence panel rocking gently on its stubby booted legs. He has no mouth, so the performance is entirely gesture and the rocking of the panel.
Wilson raises the lantern-carried server rack toward the smoking status board, holding it steady as the smoke thickens behind him, then lowers it. The smoke billows continuously through the shot.
